correctness.rationale: The source-compatible one-block dual-extrapolated proximal updates reduce exactly to a time-two Floquet map. Its characteristic trace and determinant yield three strict Schur margins; for normalized step product in (0,1), precisely one can fail. Equality has an attainable -1 eigenmode, and strict violation has an attainable eigenmode below -1. Orthogonal singular-mode decomposition proves the matrix extension and exact calculus gives the global contrast limit. A separate strictly convex-concave counterexample has an exact rational two-step characteristic polynomial negative at -1 and a nonzero exact excitation minor, proving divergence from the stated initial state. The included SymPy script reconstructs all critical identities, while the proof handles all quantifiers and boundaries.

originality.rationale: Prior 2013 and 2015 adaptive PDHG papers explicitly warn that variable steps with subcritical product can fail; existence of instability is therefore not claimed. The inspected source A-SPDHG 2023 update has a convergence theorem requiring quasi-increasing changes, but no two-periodic exact borderline. The new statement derives a necessary-and-sufficient Floquet condition for its dual-extrapolated single-block scheme, a sharp uniform all-spectrum contrast threshold, and an explicit persistent strongly convex failure. Published math records most closely related address fixed steps. Checks support a best-knowledge conclusion, with switched-operator equivalences a residual risk.
residual_risks: An earlier two-periodic switched-operator theorem may have an algebraically equivalent specialization even without PDHG terminology.
Partial inspection of the older variable-step image-restoration article does not justify a global negative novelty claim.
This is self-review; independent expert audit and exhaustive literature coverage are not performed.

value.rationale: The problem is intrinsically motivated by the original theorem requiring both a product bound and temporal regularity of the step sizes. The new classification gives an exact all-initial stability boundary, a sharp model-uniform contrast limit not attained at the maximal normalized singular value, and a fully rational strongly convex failure. This is useful for choosing permitted variation in primal-dual balancing updates; it neither repeats the known existential warning nor relies on an arbitrary finite slice.
